trigger_condition: on_tool_error fires for a run_id whose thought was already removed from storage (thought is None)
guard_snippet: if thought is None: self._inflight_run_ids.get(author, set()).discard(str(run_id)); return
potential_consequence: Stale run_id stays marked in-flight forever, permanently blocking that author's error-streak aliasing

trigger_condition: AI_AGENT_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_TOOL_ERRORS dynamic config value is set to 0 or negative
potential_consequence: Every single tool error immediately aborts the run, defeating the 'consecutive' threshold semantics

trigger_condition: _invoke_agent (used by invoke/invoke_task/generate) hits a fatal exception while in supervisor/subagent mode
guard_snippet: except Exception as e: self._supervisor_coordinator.reset(); return self._build_generation_result(...)
potential_consequence: Dangling active handoff state survives a fatal error on the invoke/generate paths; only stream() clears it

trigger_condition: _build_final_chunk previously gated agent_error/tool_errors behind include_tool_errors and formatted tool_errors per error_detail_level before every final chunk
guard_snippet: in _send_error_to_thread: if not include_tool_errors: agent_error = None; tool_errors = None; else format tool_errors via format_for_level(error_detail_level)
potential_consequence: LangGraphAgent._send_error_to_thread now unconditionally sends full agent_error/tool_errors/error_details on every agent-level error, ignoring include_tool_errors=False (the default) and error_detail_level entirely

trigger_condition: close() runs on the consumer thread between send()'s is_closed() check and the subsequent queue.put()
guard_snippet: guard the is_closed check and the put with the same lock used by close()
potential_consequence: One late item can still land in the queue right after close(), and nobody drains it anymore

trigger_condition: generator_queue.queue.get() times out (300s) while the producer agent is stuck mid-step with no chunk emitted yet
guard_snippet: cancel/signal the background agent task (not just generator_queue.close()) on timeout so it stops making tool/LLM calls
potential_consequence: The abandoned agent thread keeps running tool calls and spending LLM budget indefinitely after the client-facing stream has already ended with a timeout error

trigger_condition: a configured subagent happens to be named 'supervisor', colliding with the reserved top-level node key
guard_snippet: exclude the reserved 'supervisor'/'agent' node names from the echo-detection membership check
potential_consequence: Every genuine top-level supervisor update is mistaken for a duplicate subgraph echo and silently dropped
